title: Zip Two Words Together
statement:
You get two strings, a and b. Build a new string by taking letters in turns: the first letter of a, then the first of b, then the second of a, the second of b, and so on.

When one string runs out, append whatever is left of the other in its original order. Return the result.

examples.why: Equal lengths: the letters simply alternate, starting with a.
After h, t, i, h the first word is used up, so the rest of the second, "ere", is added as it is.
The longer word can be either one; here the tail "qrs" comes from a.

constraints: a and b contain only lowercase English letters
hints: Walk both strings with one index each, or with a single shared index.
Loop up to the length of the longer string. At each index, add a's letter if it exists, then b's letter if it exists.

explain.intuition:
Use one index i that runs up to the length of the longer string. At each step take a[i] if a still has a letter there, then b[i] if b still does. Once the shorter string is used up, only the longer one contributes, which is exactly "append the rest".

Collect the pieces in an array and join once at the end. Building with repeated += is fine at this size, but the array habit pays off when strings get long.
steps: For i from 0 to max(a.length, b.length) − 1: if i < a.length push a[i]; if i < b.length push b[i].
pitfalls: Stopping at the shorter length and dropping the tail of the longer string.
Starting with b instead of a, or appending the tail of the wrong string.

solutions.title: Two pointers
solutions.idea: Advance one pointer in each string, alternating, then copy the leftover tail.

solutions.title: One index up to the longer length
solutions.idea: At each index, take a's letter and then b's letter when they exist.

followups: Zip k strings in turn instead of two.
Given the zipped result and the length of a, recover both original strings.
